first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and memory_31/memory_86 show a durable, low-risk lift from simplifying onboarding for SMB self-serve accounts—directly addressing the observed decline without the retention tradeoff seen in promotional pricing (memory_73), which I verify given the competitive pressure to match entry pricing. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) are valid but don't address this quarter's acute onboarding/activation drop. With only one experiment slot, I'm prioritizing the intervention with the clearest causal link to the current metrics and no known downstream harm. I verified memory_73 specifically because the competitor pricing pressure creates temptation to override its retention warning, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-activation link before committing scarce capacity. Running as a standard (not broad) experiment preserves optionality to pivot to sales-assist or referral incentives next cycle if enterprise or established-customer segments need attention.
